opportunities.title: US-34: Release cash reward to finder
opportunities.description:
### Epic: E8 | Track: Staff | Story Points: 3

**User Story:**
As office staff, I want to record when unclaimed cash is handed to its finder after six months, so the item leaves my held list and the payout is on record.

**Acceptance Criteria (Given-When-Then):**
- Given a held cash item past its reward date, when I confirm the finder's identity and record the payout, then the item is marked as paid to the finder, separately from "released to owner", along with who received it, the ID they showed, the staff member and the time.
- Given a cash item whose reward date hasn't arrived, when I try to record a finder payout, then it is refused.
- Given the payout is recorded, then the item drops out of the staff reminders and the held-items list, and stays out of public search.
- Given another office holds the item, when I try to record the payout, then it is refused.

opportunities.title: Intake creates item entries for coins, cash-equivalent treasure and cash quest rewards
opportunities.description:
## Problem
Session 6 Delta Review proposed a NEW `inventory_and_loot` item for every stated amount in one treasure hoard: "New Item — 1,400 cp", "— 1,300 sp", "— 70 gp", "— Art and Gems (9…)". Campaign Manager is not an inventory system: only distinct things of significance become items.

## Cause
- `NARRATIVE_EXTRACT_SYSTEM` rule 6 in `shared/chronicle-ai.js` tells the AI to include coins and to use "one entry per denomination", with `"1400 cp"` as its example.
- The mixed-page schema in `fillRoundsFromText()` describes items as `"<item or coin name>"`.
- `_processNarrativeResult()` in `admin/delta-review.html` turns every `result.items` entry into a NEW item.
- The redesign pipeline has the same gap: the step 2 "thing" definition in `shared/chronicle-entities.js` is "a notable object or treasure", and step 4 loot facts in `shared/chronicle-facts.js` have no rule.
- `docs/intake-redesign.md` lists "coins found" as an example of a Thing.

## Rule
- **Cash or cash equivalent, never an item:** coins, currency, payments, and any gem, art object or treasure with a stated cash value ("emerald worth 100 GP", "2 smoky quartz, 25 GP each", "art and gems").
  - **As a quest reward:** a narrative note on the quest, written as the notes state it ("Rewarded 200 GP and an emerald worth 30 GP"), with `reward_received.value_gp` set to the total stated value (230). No item entry, no `item_refs`.
  - **Found any other way:** narrative in the session (`session_notes` / passages).
- **Possible item:** a gem or object described by something other than its price, with no value given ("oddly warm gem", "shimmering diamond"). Proposed for the DM to confirm.
- **Always an item:** named or magic items (Immovable Rod, +1 Moon Sickle) and quest objects (maps, letters, keys).

## Approach
- Rewrite rule 6 and the mixed-page items schema to the rule above; route treasure into `session_notes` and quest rewards into the quest.
- Apply the same rule to step 2 "thing" mentions and step 4 loot facts.
- Client-side guard in `_processNarrativeResult()` that drops currency-only or priced-pile names the AI still returns, and adds them to the page summary as narrative so nothing is lost.
- Fix the "coins found" example in `docs/intake-redesign.md`.
- Tests: guard cases (cp/sp/gp amounts, "Art and Gems (…)", priced gems) vs kept items (Silver Dagger, Golden Idol, Potion of Healing ×2, oddly warm gem); prompt text for all four paths.

## Done when
- Re-interpreting the session 6 hoard page proposes no coin, priced-gem or pile items, and the treasure appears as narrative.
- A quest page with a cash reward adds a narrative note and `value_gp` on the quest, and no item.
- Named items and unpriced distinctive objects still come through.

## Related data cleanup (done directly, not by this issue)
- Remove `item_009` "Trade Commission" and its refs (session_004 `items_found`, qst_004 `reward_received.item_refs`).
- Remove `item_010` "Unrefined Emerald" and its refs (session_005 `items_found` and `key_moments[1].ref`, qst_005 `reward_received.item_refs`). Item says Helen paid it, qst_005 says Krustie Gnome — confirm which before removing.

opportunities.title: Referral reward: give a month, get a month
opportunities.description:
**Why:** at $20/mo and about $14 gross margin, a free month for a successful referral costs about $5.80 in AI spend (we're not paying cash, just serving chapters). That's far cheaper than a paid-ad CAC, so rewards should be generous and simple.

**Proposed mechanic (confirm before building)**
- Referrer: **1 free month** for every referred family that subscribes (cap 6 months).
- Referred: **first month free** (or 50% off). Pick one for the test; don't run both.
- Credit applied through Stripe (customer balance / coupon). No cash, no points.
- Reward fires on the referred family's first paid invoice, not on signup. This prevents abuse where people sign up just to get previews.

**Abuse guards:** one reward per phone number, self-referral blocked (same device/phone), cap per referrer.

**Depends on:** billing, referral attribution.

**Acceptance:** a test referral from family A subscribing credits family A's next invoice.

opportunities.title: Competitions: award cash, reputation and honours exactly once
opportunities.description:
Part of #323. Source: [Career progression, competitions and rewards](https://app.notion.com/p/4150870d4c44810c880ae3395086e9d0?pvs=204), CPP-07; CPP-06 payout outcomes.

**Delivery outcome:** A.

**Prerequisites:** #570, #571, #559

## Work

- Implement saved reward identities and one atomic award path for competition cash, reputation, honours and future entitlement records.
- Connect the Open Cup's published progression prizes and neutral/home income rules to FIN-04; distinguish ordinary fixture cash from extra round prizes and never pay a bye.
- Store honours with season, competition, club and winning squad. Definition snapshots preserve promised rewards if catalogue data changes later.
- Persist reward state through result replay, report reopening, save/load, held-match recovery and rollover. Leave earned cap calculation to the cap integration issue.

**Done when:** Cash/reputation/honours reconcile with recorded outcomes and the published prize table, every award is applied once, and duplicate completion/reload/report opening cannot grant another reward or alter an existing trophy.

## Validation

Award idempotency, normal and cancelled fixtures, no-bye rewards, neutral income splitting, cap-entitlement records with no premature activation and failure with no partial application.

## Likely code areas

Existing finance/money and result ownership operations; state reward/honour records and season statistics/history.

## Delivery

Follow current AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, state ownership and save-recovery contracts. One focused change per PR (split the ticket if implementation reveals separate deliverables); required TypeScript/Vitest/build, CI/QA and an independent checker for implementation. Update repository hub and the Notion spec when behaviour lands. Keep .github workflows, Android manual dispatch, monetisation and unrelated match-rule changes outside this ticket. Coordinate shared state/save/time files sequentially with the finance and progression work. Issue creation records planned work, not implementation, test evidence or merge permission.

opportunities.title: Bug: Kraken staking rewards display $0.00 despite received crypto value
opportunities.description:
## Before you start (required)

### General checklist

- [x] I have removed personal / sensitive data from screenshots and logs
- [x] I have searched [existing issues](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/issues?q=is:issue) and [discussions](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/discussions) for this symptom and found no exact duplicate

### How are you using Sure?

- [ ] I was a paying Maybe customer (hosted version)
- [ ] I use it on PikaPod, Umbrel or similar (VPS included)
- [x] I am a self-hosted user (local only)

### Self hoster checklist

_Paying, hosted users should delete this entire section._

- Self hosted app commit SHA (find in user menu): **Not supplied yet — using the `stable` Docker image; will update from user menu**
  - [ ] I have confirmed that my app's commit is the latest version of Sure
- Where are you hosting?
  - [ ] Render
  - [x] Docker Compose
  - [ ] Umbrel
  - [ ] PikaPod
  - [ ] Other (please specify)

---

## Bug description

Kraken staking rewards are imported as `Trade` entries with a positive crypto quantity, a historical unit price, an activity label of `Dividend` (or `Interest` for Earn), and **zero cash movement**. That last part is correct for balance accounting, but the transaction list and trade detail header render the zero cash movement as **$0.00**, which misleadingly makes the reward appear worthless even when crypto was received.

The real value of the received units is `quantity × recorded unit price` in the trade's currency (historical at the date of receipt), if pricing data is available.

The importer intentionally sets `Entry#amount = 0` in `KrakenAccount::LedgerProcessor#create_crypto_trade` to avoid phantom cash. The problem is in **presentation**: `app/views/trades/_trade.html.erb` and `app/views/trades/_header.html.erb` always display `entry.amount_money`, rather than a separately labelled non-cash reward valuation.

This is distinct from #2450 (importing Kraken ledger events) and #3875 (preventing phantom cash in Kraken crypto movements). Neither should be undone.

### To Reproduce

1. Connect a Kraken account with ledger-reading permission and sync it in Sure.
2. Receive an ETH staking reward (or other crypto reward).
3. Go to the connected Kraken account's transaction history.
4. Find `Staking reward <quantity> ETH`, marked `Dividend`.
5. Observe `$0.00` at the right of the transaction row, and again in the trade detail header, despite a positive received quantity and available price.

### Expected behavior

Show the historical **estimated value received** (recorded `trade.qty × trade.price`, in `trade.currency`) for Kraken crypto staking/Earn rewards, visibly marked as a **non-cash value**. Preserve `entry.amount = 0` and existing holdings/balance calculations. Do not invent a fiat cash deposit.

If the imported price is unavailable or flagged as missing, show an unavailable value rather than a misleading `$0.00` or an unreliable spot-price fallback. Ordinary buys, sells, transfers and manually entered cash dividends should continue to display their actual monetary amounts.

### Screenshots and/or recordings

A screenshot of the connected Kraken transaction list shows positive ETH reward quantities, a `Dividend` label and `$0.00` values. It is not attached here to avoid exposing personal financial data; a redacted screenshot can be added if needed.

opportunities.title: MP-V8 · Product validation: Buy crypto with cash: code first, then cash
opportunities.description:
> **How to submit:** apply through the Drips bot. Once **assigned**, copy [`docs/validation/TEMPLATE.md`](https://github.com/Micopay/micopay-protocol/blob/main/docs/validation/TEMPLATE.md) to `docs/validation/responses/MP-V8.md`, fill it in and open a **PR that only adds that file**. Rules: [`docs/validation/README.md`](https://github.com/Micopay/micopay-protocol/blob/main/docs/validation/README.md).

**Drips research task** · `complexity: low` · **one assignee**.

### What we want to learn

Whether the **deposit** flow (you hand over cash, you receive crypto) is clear, including "**code first, then cash**" and the "**I paid and they didn’t confirm**" button. And whether you see **potential for MicoPay in your country**.

This is a **short test on testnet**, not a full trade: no real money moves and there are no cash agents online yet. When a step needs another person, stop there and tell us what you understood.

### What you need

- The app: **https://app.micopay.com.mx**
- A browser on a computer or a phone.
- The **Varial** wallet on **testnet**. It is the only wallet the web app supports today.

### Your task

1. Write step 1 of the template before signing in.
2. Sign in with **Varial on testnet** and start a **deposit** (buy crypto with cash).
3. Go as far as the app lets you. When it needs an agent on the other side, **stop** and read the screen you are on.
4. Fill in the rest of the template.

### Questions for this issue

- Is it clear when you should hand over the cash, and when you should not yet?
- What do you think happens if you press "I paid and they didn’t confirm"? Does it give you confidence?
- What would worry you about handing cash to a stranger, and what would calm you down?

Section **5. Your country** of the template is the same for every issue. Please answer it too.

### Privacy first

opportunities.title: CryptoEnv.reset() retains accumulated reward from the previous episode
opportunities.description:
`CryptoEnv.reset()` restores cash, holdings and total assets but leaves `gamma_return` and `episode_return` unchanged. `step()` continues accumulating into the old `gamma_return` and returns that accumulator at termination. Later episodes therefore receive reward from earlier episodes.

Reproduced at `5df023ed3faab4cb529bc7e2837a7fb331067cf2` with synthetic data and no market-data requests:

```python
import numpy as np
from finrl.meta.env_cryptocurrency_trading.env_multiple_crypto import CryptoEnv

prices = np.array([[100.0], [100.0], [110.0], [120.0], [100.0]])
env = CryptoEnv(
    {"price_array": prices, "tech_array": np.zeros_like(prices)},
    initial_capital=1000.0, buy_cost_pct=0.0, sell_cost_pct=0.0,
)
env.reset()
for action in (0.01, 0.0, 0.0):
    _, reward, done, _ = env.step(np.array([action]))
print(reward)  # 0.00030364990234375

env.reset()
for _ in range(env.max_step):
    _, reward, done, _ = env.step(np.array([0.0]))
print(env.total_asset, reward)  # 1000.0, 0.00029463119659423824
```

Expected: the second episode's reward is zero because it holds only cash throughout. Resetting during an unfinished episode also retains its accumulated reward.

Proposed fix: reset `gamma_return` and `episode_return` to their constructor values in `reset()`. I have a focused patch with regression tests for gains, losses, different discount factors, repeated identical episodes and mid-episode resets.

AI assistance was used to investigate the bug, prepare the patch and run the regression tests.

opportunities.title: Issue Refunds immediately, for the amount paid
opportunities.description:
Blocked by: #2

## Problem
- An eligible request only stores a `refunds` row with status `requested` (`app/routes/courses.$slug.refund.ts:216-223`).
- Nothing ever approves it, returns money, or ends the Enrollment.
- The amount uses the list price unless the Purchase was discounted (`app/routes/courses.$slug.refund.ts:206`, `app/routes/courses.$slug.tsx:492`). The email calls that "the amount you paid", while Settings shows `amountPaid`.

## Scenario
Liam paid $79, and the Instructor later reprices the course to $99. His email promises "$99, the amount you paid".

## Expected behavior
A Refund takes effect immediately. The Learner gets back exactly the amount they paid, and their Enrollment ends.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The Refund is recorded with the amount equal to `amountPaid` and a timestamp.
- [ ] The Enrollment ends, and the Learner can no longer open the course's lessons.
- [ ] The confirmation email states the amount paid. It's still only logged, because no mail transport exists.
- [ ] No more `requested` or "pending" state. The schema is simplified with a migration and the seed updated.
- [ ] The Learner lands on a page showing what was refunded.
- [ ] Tests cover the repricing scenario.

## Out of scope
A real payment provider (none exists), and refunds for Team Purchases (#12).

opportunities.title: Paid subscriptions
opportunities.description:
## User story

As a writer, I want to charge for a paid tier through my own Stripe account, so that I keep the revenue minus Stripe's fees.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The owner connects their own Stripe account, and the project adds no fee of its own
- [ ] Readers pay through Stripe Checkout on a monthly or yearly price
- [ ] A Stripe webhook sets the subscriber's tier and paid-through date, and handles cancellations, refunds and failed payments
- [ ] A post can be marked paid-only. The web page shows a preview with a paywall, and the email goes to paying readers only
- [ ] Paying readers sign in on the web with an emailed link to read paid posts
- [ ] The preference center links to Stripe's customer portal
- [ ] Tests replay Stripe's webhook events for each case

## Who does the work

- **Apso generates:** the tier fields and storage for plans and payments.
- **Stripe provides:** checkout, billing and the customer portal.
- **Hand-written:** the Stripe webhook, the paywall, reader sign-in and the paying-reader segment.

## Estimate

**Size L.** It adds a second kind of user, a payment provider and gated content.

The README defines the sizes. They are estimates, since nothing here has been built.

## Notes and sources

- Substack's page says "Writers keep 90% of their revenue minus credit card fees." Beehiiv and Ghost say they take no cut of paid subscriptions, per [docs/reference-products.md](../blob/main/docs/reference-products.md).
- No paid service is set up until the owner asks for this issue.

## Depends on

#14, #17, #19

opportunities.title: Epic: Newsletter module (subscribers, delivery, tracking, analytics, paid issues)
opportunities.description:
## Goal

A creator, and Genfeed itself, runs a full newsletter from app.genfeed.ai: write or generate an issue, send it to subscribers in the brand's own look, see who opened and clicked, and charge for it in GEN credits. One module, one place in the app, no outside newsletter tool.

Document only. The week of 11-09 is a coding lock; nothing here starts until Vincent gives the go.

## Today (verified in code at master `e39a197c`)

- Authoring exists: `Newsletter` model with generation, approval, schedule (`packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma`), API at `collections/newsletters`, editor under `apps/web/app/(protected)/[orgSlug]/[brandSlug]/edit/newsletter`.
- Delivery today is only to a connected third-party publication (`long-form-deliveries.service.ts`). Genfeed never emails an issue itself.
- `renderNewsletterHtml` turns Markdown into sanitized HTML. There is **no email layout**: no brand logo, banner, colors, footer or plain-text part.
- Resend sends our own mail one message at a time (`apps/server/notifications/src/services/resend/resend.service.ts`). No batch, no audience.
- Delivery analytics exist for system mail: `EmailMessage` (accepted, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced, complained), first-party `EmailClick`, signed Resend webhook, suppression list (`email-performance.service.ts`). They are tied to a registered `userId`, so they cannot yet cover outside subscribers.
- No subscriber model, no subscribe endpoint, no CSV import. The marketing footer's newsletter block links to a third-party sign-up page.
- Brand has colors, font, watermark logo ids and an end card; `BANNER` exists as an asset category (`asset.enum.ts`). No dedicated newsletter header fields.

## Recommendation

Yes, make it a module. The pieces share one subscriber table, one send pipeline and one analytics store, and splitting them across the article, profile and credits work would duplicate all three. The module is one app section (Issues, Subscribers, Analytics, Settings) over three API modules: subscribers, sends, analytics.

## Scope and existing issues

| Area | Issue |
| --- | --- |
| Creator profile URLs and showcase | #9662, #9661 (under #9666) |
| Public subscribe, subscriber model, double opt-in, first send | #9665 (under #9666) |
| Credits ledger, tips, paid subscriptions, paid issues, earnings, cash-out decision | #9715 to #9720 (under #9714) |
| App section and module boundaries | new, linked below |
| Subscriber management: add by email, CSV import and export | new |
| Email template and brand identity | new |
| Bulk delivery engine | new (carves the engine out of #9665) |
| Tracking and analytics | new |
| Genfeed's own newsletter: homepage, footer, archive | new |
| Remove third-party newsletter platform references | new |

## Order

1. Decisions below.
2. #9662 URLs, then subscriber model and subscribe flow (#9665 first half).
3. Subscriber management in the app (add, CSV).
4. Email template and brand identity.
5. Bulk delivery engine, then tracking and analytics.
6. Genfeed's own newsletter on the homepage, then the reference cleanup (needs a working sign-up before the old link goes).
7. Credits: #9715, #9716, #9717, #9718, #9719. #9720 is a decision, not a build.

## Decisions needed before building

- Sending domain: shared Genfeed domain first, or each brand verifies its own.
- Plan limits: subscribers and sends per month per plan (Cloud runtime gate).
- Platform fee on paid issues (from #9714).
- Whether the existing connected-publication delivery stays as an optional target.
- Whether CSV import needs a per-import consent confirmation (recommended: yes).

## Done when

A visitor subscribes on Genfeed's homepage, confirms by email, and receives the next issue in Genfeed's look; the owner imports a CSV in the app; the issue shows opens and clicks; a paid issue is unlocked with credits. Each sub-issue has its own finish condition and evidence.

opportunities.title: Complete #3714 native bug-issue paid-label guard acceptance

Five natural issues (#3729, #3732, #3751, #3752 and #3753) also have actual owner additions and bot removals of `devin-ready`, paired with bot comments whose first line is `(aside)` and that name the six missing premises. Their complete label-event histories contain no `bug` label. The scratch bug issue #3731 has no `devin-ready` event. This establishes real guard effects, but not the exact native bug-with-Verification repeat. It does not establish that this branch has never worked or that the guard is defective.

Current verification passed 225 cases across the complete Actions-gate, shared-reader and plan-hook modules plus the changed importer-parity test. Another 314 independent original/current observations include actual script processes using an owned `gh` executable, verified-bug and opposite cases, fresh-state reads, failure propagation and first-write ordering. These are controlled mechanism evidence, not the missing native receipt.

## Acceptance

- Prefer recovering retained, attributable GitHub Actions evidence for the bug case during ordinary authorized work. If a new trial is necessary, an operator must first have explicit authorization for its label, possible paid-session and spending effects. This issue itself authorizes no paid launch or new application of `devin-ready`.
- For a `bug` issue with five complete Verification answers but missing the six premise answers, confirm the real workflow removes `devin-ready` and posts the missing-six comment with `(aside)` on its first line. Confirm `premises-missing` follows the bug's Verification section independently of that paid-label decision.
- Retain an opposite case showing that complete premise answers allow the paid label to remain, while the bug's own missing-label status still follows Verification. Recover existing evidence where possible; close any authorized scratch issues after the trial.
- Record the actual workflow/code revision, issue, relevant run/job or label-event identifiers and comment links. Do not infer a run head from a bot comment. Add the evidence to #3714's verification obligation and read back its result.

The owner already accepted that the external integration can start before the guard removes the label. Preserve that stated limit. This task does not request a preventive hook, an atomic-startup guarantee, or a new guard design. #4045 is a separate native plan-approval acceptance task; #4182's token-created issue-label fix and #4158's later test failures do not supply this receipt.

## Premise checks

2. Searched issues in all states for #3714, premise-gate and devin-ready acceptance, and read the related tasks. The two scratch issues are closed, #4045 concerns native plan approval, and no existing task found owns this native bug-guard repeat.
3. Keep this verification only. Reuse the existing workflow, parser and evidence record; do not redesign the accepted post-label control or relax its six-premise requirement.
4. The consumer is the repository's issue-triggered premise-gate workflow. An operator authorized for the possible paid integration effect can recover evidence or qualify a suitable ordinary event. The original post-merge obligation remains open until that acceptance is established or the owner explicitly accepts an equivalent.
5. Counts are fresh retained populations: 225 current test cases, 314 independent observations, two scratch label roundtrips and five natural guard removals. They are not failure rates or a full repository-event census.

opportunities.title: feat(paid): paid read gate over a recorded exclusion view
opportunities.description:
## Context

D-010 (filter now, purge on rebuild) requires that a recorded opt-out withdrawal applies at once on every paid read path, held providers and sessions included. The rule and its probe are in §1.2 of the tessera-boundary document; the code does not exist. The paid tier is not part of the stage-0 build, so this issue has no milestone until a hosted-tier milestone exists.

## Proposal

- Implement `PaidTier` as the only holder of paid scopes and `PaidServing` as the paid service's only input: filtered batches, leaf `GuardedExec` providers, streams, sessions without DDL and guarded crops.
- Implement the exclusion view: source and item verdicts, cycle completions and per-generation admissions in one hash-chained log with its head in keep; `admitted(generation)` and `not withdrawn(now)` per scan and per batch.
- Add one conformance case per paid read path, as listed in §5.

## Acceptance

- [ ] **TEST-151** (DES-057), as specified in the design's verification table: 0 rows of a withdrawn source (recorded `OptedOut`, cycle complete or not), a reserved item or an item with no verdict on any path after the withdrawal, held providers, sessions, streams, crops and derived rows included; 0 rows of a source allowed, or allowed again, after the generation's admission until its rebuild, on every path; a withdrawal between an admission and a refresh filtered; only batches inside `exclusion_max_age` may still carry one, and they are counted; every compile-fail case fails with its pinned code.
- [ ] **TEST-152** (DES-058), as specified in the design's verification table: every fault is `Integrity` before any row is served; a generation without an admission is `Refused`; a missing verdict excludes its rows; a scan created after a withdrawal never serves it; no batch after `max_age` serves it.
- [ ] Every node under **Delivers** keeps its `delivered_by` edge to this issue in `docs/traceability/edges.json`.

**Delivers:** DES-057, DES-058, TEST-151, TEST-152.

Design: [docs/architecture/tessera-boundary.md](https://github.com/nerdmachines/scitadel-hub/blob/dev/docs/architecture/tessera-boundary.md) §1.2 — DES-057, DES-058 ([traceability](https://github.com/nerdmachines/scitadel-hub/blob/dev/docs/traceability/README.md)).

opportunities.title: Epic: Creator earnings in GEN credits (tips, paid subscriptions, paid articles)
opportunities.description:
## Goal

Readers can pay creators in GEN credits, and creators spend what they earn on generation inside Genfeed. This completes the creator publishing loop started in #9666: write, publish, email subscribers (#9665), get paid.

Document only. The week of 11-09 is a coding lock, so no code is scheduled.

## Today (verified in code at master `e0d9b108`)

- `CreditBalance` and `CreditTransaction` belong to an organization or billing account, never to a user (`packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma`).
- Transaction categories are `add`, `deduct`, `expire`, `reset`, `rollover`, `refund`, `byok-usage` (`packages/contracts/src/enums/credit.enum.ts`). There is **no transfer between accounts**, no tip, no paid subscription to a creator.
- Stripe is used only for Genfeed's own plans (`Subscription`, `UserSubscription`). No Stripe Connect and no payout code.
- `Article` and `Newsletter` have no price or access fields. Every published article is public.

## Scope

Earn-and-spend only: earned credits are spent on generation inside Genfeed and are not withdrawable. This avoids payouts, KYC and tax handling. Cash-out is a separate decision (see the last issue).

## Order

1. Credit transfer ledger (everything else builds on it).
2. Tips.
3. Paid subscriptions to a creator.
4. Paid articles and newsletter issues.
5. Creator earnings view.
6. Decision: cash-out.

## Decisions needed before building

- Platform fee on each payment (percentage, or none at first).
- Whether earned credits expire like purchased ones, or never expire.
- Whether earned credits count toward plan limits and the low-credits banner.
- Who can pay: signed-in Genfeed users only, or a guest checkout that creates an account.

## Done when

A reader with credits tips a creator, subscribes to them, and unlocks a paid article. The creator's balance rises by the amount minus the fee, and the creator spends it on a generation. Each sub-issue carries its own finish condition and evidence.

opportunities.title: [bounty] math module tour
opportunities.description:
Hi! I'd like to claim the **$25 recurring micro-bounty: "write a blog post tutorial for any single stdlib module"** for `stdlib/math.ltl`.

## Deliverables

- `docs/blog/math-module-tour.ltlml` — tutorial
- `examples/math_tour.ltl` — runnable companion program with 26 pinned test vectors

## What the tutorial covers

- The import form that actually works (`from stdlib.math import ...`, not `import math`)
- 26 exact pinned vectors in a table, each asserted by the companion program
- Four traps: `floor`/`ceil` rounding toward ±infinity (`floor(-2.5) == -3`), `clamp` returning `float`, `sign(0) == 0`, and `log` being the natural log
- Float-pinning rules: exact literals for `sqrt`/`log`/`exp`, but `sin(PI / 6.0) == 0.49999999999999994`, so trig should not be pinned at non-trivial angles
- The callable-surface finding: 12 of `math.ltl`'s 24 declared functions bind on the Python backend, `log`/`exp` are undeclared yet callable, and `ln`/`log2`/`log10` are declared yet unbound — the tutorial pins what actually works instead of documenting the declaration list

## Verification

```bash
python3 -m lateralus_lang run examples/math_tour.ltl
#   26 passed, 0 failed  (26 vectors)

python3 -m lateralus_lang check examples/math_tour.ltl
#   OK
```

Both were run from the repo root on `main` (lateralus-lang 3.2.0, Python 3.14).

PR: #266 (`xilin2020:bounty/math-module-tour`, signed-off commit). Happy to split or reword anything; `stdlib/math.ltl` is otherwise left untouched.

```
chacha20 32aa25005fe5f3a9:b1bffb37
aho_corasick 751
radix_sort_u32 000017df:ffffe0a8:5301c95d
```

Correctness is pinned to published vectors, not just cross-language agreement:
xxh64("") = `ef46db3751d8e999`, xxh64("abc") = `44bc2cf5ad770999`,
xxh64("Nobody inspects the spammish repetition") = `fbcea83c8a378bf1`,
adler32("Wikipedia") = `11e60398`, and the ChaCha20 block matches RFC 8439
§2.4.2 (asserted at startup in both languages, not just documented).

Two real bugs were found and fixed while pinning this: the Python LZ4 bucket
hash wasn't wrapping to 32 bits (so it disagreed with the JS crawler), and the
ChaCha20 state had the nonce in the wrong words.

Next: inline `stdlib/{xxhash,lz4,aho_corasick,radix_sort}` + `std/crypto/chacha20`
into one self-contained `.ltl` source with a driver, run the Lateralus side, and
commit `benchmarks/results/stdlib_results.md` with all three languages.
